# ACC006 `missing-acc-routine`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A project procedure is called inside an OpenACC compute region but has no `!$acc routine`.

## Why

Code executed on the device can only call procedures compiled for the device: each needs an
`!$acc routine` directive (with its parallelism level, usually `seq`). Without it the compiler
either fails, or inlines the call only when it can see the body, so the build breaks as soon as
the procedure moves to another file or the optimisation level changes.

## Reported

```fortran
!$acc parallel loop
do i = 1, n
  call flux_cell(q(:, i))      ! flux_cell has no !$acc routine
end do
```

## Preferred

```fortran
subroutine flux_cell(q)
  !$acc routine seq
  ...
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[ACC006] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = ACC006` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).
